title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: genus 0, I a 4-element set. Grothendieck is building a 'tangentially framed' version of the genus-0 Teichmüller groupoid. In modern terms this is the space of I-pointed P^1's together with a nonzero tangent vector at each marked point.

(1) From the previous page: Σ_J = P(V(J)), where V(J) = ker(O^J → O, sum). For |J| = 3 this is a P^1. It serves as the compactification \hat M_{0,I} ≅ \bar M_{0,4} ≅ P^1, with three boundary sections α' (α ∈ J). The open part is Σ_I^* ≅ M_{0,I} = P^1 minus 3 points. In this reading J is the 3-element set of boundary degenerations (pair-partitions of I). The previous page left an ambiguity. For the line bundle T_i, the tangent line of the universal I-marked curve X along the section i, one has \hat T_i ≅ O(1) ⊗_Z L(ω), and two cases were open:
- L(ω) = Z, functorial in (J, i);
- L(ω) = Z(ω), the sign twist by an orientation ω ∈ ord(J).

(2) Restricting to a boundary section α' gives T_i|_{α'} ≅ O_{α'}(1) ⊗ L(ω). Since O_{α'}(1) ≅ O ⊗ Z(ω) (the determinant computation of the previous page), this is O ⊗ (Z(ω) ⊗ L(ω)).

(3) Independently, a 'square structure' Q on I with a marked vertex i gives a marked degeneration, i.e. a tangential base point. There the stable curve's description trivialises T_i up to the same sign twist: T_i ≅ O ⊗ Z(ω), with ω(Q) ≅ ω. Comparing the two gives L(ω) = Z. Hence the boxed result: \hat T_i ≅ O(1) canonically, functorially in i. It is also identified with F̌(ω), the dual of the kernel F in 0 → F → O(I) → O(1) → 0.

(4) Let \hat P_i be the G_m-torsor of nonzero tangent vectors at i. Their fibre product SP̂_I = ∏_{/M} \hat P_i is a G_m^I-torsor. All factors are the same torsor V^*(O(1)) (the complement of the zero section). So SP̂_I is the pushout of V^*(O(1)) along the diagonal G_m → G_m^I. Restricting to the open stratum gives SP_I ≅ (V^*(O(1)) | Σ_I^*) ∧_{G_m} G_m^I.

(5) Over C, analytically, take π_1. The framed Teichmüller group is S𝒯_{0,I} ≅ π_1(V^*(O(1)) | Σ_I^*) ∧_Z Z^I, the pushout of the central Z along the diagonal Z → Z^I. Concretely, V^*(O(±1)) over P^1 minus 3 points is C^2 minus 3 lines through 0. Its π_1 is the pure braid group P_3 ≅ F_2 × Z. Hence S𝒯_{0,4} ≅ (F_2 × Z) ∧_Z Z^4 ≅ F_2 × Z^4. This is the pure mapping class group of a sphere with 4 boundary circles: F_2 extended centrally by the 4 boundary Dehn twists. The next page goes on to study PΣ_I^* and S_0𝒯_{0,4}.
errors: Possible sign/convention issue. On \bar M_{0,4} the cotangent line at a marked point has degree ψ_i = 1, so the tangent line (normal bundle of the section) has degree -1. The boxed '\hat T_i ≅ O(1)' is correct only if O(1) on Σ_I = P(V(I)) is meant in a dual convention, or if \hat T_i denotes something other than the plain extended tangent line. The equivalent '≅ F̌(ω)' also suggests dualisation. The torsor-level conclusion is unaffected, since V^*(L) and V^*(L^{-1}) have isomorphic total spaces.

The rank and index bookkeeping (Σ_I vs Σ_J, O(I) of rank 4 vs a rank-2 sequence for F to be a line bundle) is loose on the page. It is only consistent if the relevant set has 3 elements (the boundary points), or if F is not of rank 1.

ideas.what: Using tangential base points (square structures / marked degenerations) to fix a sign ambiguity L(ω) ∈ {Z, Z(ω)} in the identification of the tangent line bundle at a marked point over \bar M_{0,4}.
ideas.modern_name: tangential base points; ψ-class line bundles on \bar M_{0,n}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1989) for tangential base points; ψ-classes to Mumford/Witten/Kontsevich era
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses base points at infinity and the Teichmüller tower only informally

ideas.what: Framed moduli space: the G_m^I-torsor of nonzero tangent vectors at the marked points, identified for |I|=4 as the diagonal pushout of the tautological G_m-torsor over P^1 minus 3 points.
ideas.modern_name: moduli of pointed curves with tangent vectors / decorated (framed) M_{0,n}
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (e.g. Ihara, Nakamura, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps; Bar-Natan for braid/GT parenthesised versions)

ideas.what: S𝒯_{0,4} ≅ π_1(C^2 minus 3 lines) ∧_Z Z^4 ≅ F_2 × Z^4, the mapping class group of a 4-holed sphere with boundary twists central.
ideas.modern_name: pure mapping class group of S_{0,4} with boundary; P_3 ≅ F_2 × Z
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions Teichmüller groups of surfaces with boundary/holes in the tower

deep.surprise_reason: A careful, canonical (sign-correct) algebro-geometric construction of the boundary-framed genus-0 Teichmüller group for n=4. It is nicely done, with the comparison via square structures fixing the twist. The results themselves (ψ-line bundle, P_3 = F_2 × Z, F_2 × Z^4) are standard and appear in the later Grothendieck–Teichmüller literature.
transcription_corrections: 'courbe[?] proj. relative' is plausibly 'courbe proj. relative', i.e. the relative projective I-marked curve X; fits context.
'structure carrée[?]' looks right (square drawn with corner i); 'dégénérescence[?] marquée' also plausible.
In the S𝒯 formula the group symbol is π_1 (written like a stylised Π_1), and the pushout is over Z into Z^I.
